text:
Support - Sam: heads up — Customer cust-193 reporting large p99 latency spikes for API requests from APAC -> us-west routing since ~08:12 UTC. Multiple reports, one repro attached: curl -w '%{time_starttransfer}\n' -s -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -> 1.8s (normally ~120ms).

oncall-bot: alert: p99_latency > 1200ms for route: apac->us-west (cluster: edge-eu-apac). Incident ID 2025-04-12-01

Anna (SRE): copying in eng-networking. Sam, can you paste the customer's request headers + SNI and an example IP?

Support - Sam: sent DM with client IP 203.45.12.88 and SNI api.redwood.example, timestamped logs -> RFC 3339 snippet in DM. Customer says traceroute shows an extra hop through an unknown ASN.

Ryan M: ran quick probe from our apac-probe:
```
traceroute -n -w 1 -q 1 203.45.12.88
1  10.0.0.1  1.1 ms
2  198.51.100.5  14 ms
3  203.0.113.25  120 ms  <-- unexpected cross-zone hop
4  198.51.100.10 130 ms
```
looks like traffic is hairpinned via partner ASN 203.0.113.0/24 causing ~100ms extra.

Mitra: timeline check — we had a peering config rollout to partner-net yesterday at 07:30 UTC that modified GSLB weight for apac pop -> us-west2. Could be accidental anycast shift. Checking BGP / GSLB logs.

Infra Eng - Lee: I see the same in our route-change audit: weight(apac->us-west2) incremented by 20% at 07:31 by deploy 2025-04-11-tnr. Rolling back that change might restore normal path.

Anna (SRE): before rollback, can we confirm TLS handshake timings? Customer mentioned slow TTFB on first byte, which often indicates TCP/TLS path issues. Sam — ask customer to run:
```
openssl s_time -connect api.redwood.example:443 -new -reconnect
```
and/or `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:203.45.12.88 https://api.redwood.example/v1/health` and paste TLS debug snippet.

Support - Sam: customer posted curl -v: shows TCP connect 30ms, but TLS handshake stalled at "ServerHello" for ~900ms.

Ryan M: aligns with extra egress hop causing handshake RTT inflation. Hypothesis: partner's middlebox is queueing or doing deep inspection.

Mitra: starting a quick mitigation — will revert GSLB weight change to previous value for apac pop to us-west2 and force lower weight -> us-west (us-west1) to re-steer. Oncall-bot will run probes to validate.

oncall-bot: action: run synthetic probes every 30s for apac->us-west endpoints.

Infra Eng - Lee: reverting now (deploy 2025-04-12-08:25UTC): set weight(apac->us-west2)=previous; flush local DNS TTLs.

Anna (SRE): also add a temporary routing rule to pin cust-193 to us-west1 at the edge config (route override) so their session doesn't flip mid-request. Steps:
```
edgectl route-override add --customer cust-193 --region us-west1 --ttl 600
```

Ryan M: running pings and curl probes after rollback: p99 from apac probe -> us-west1 dropped to 180ms within two minutes. Customer confirmed improvement: their sample request now 140ms.

Support - Sam: customer reports SLA back within normal range, thanks team.

Mitra: creating follow-up ticket to revert temporary route-override after partner fix and to schedule rollback verification with partner. Also flag for postmortem: internal rollout didn't include partner-impact checklist.

Anna (SRE): next steps:
- Mitra to open postmortem (link placeholder) and coordinate partner rollback
- Infra to add quick pre-merge check for GSLB weight changes that touch apac-pop mappings
- DevEx to notify support playbook with troubleshooting steps and commands we used (traceroute, curl, openssl).

Infra Eng - Lee: logs show p99 spike correlated with our roll at 07:31 -> roll back at 08:25 reduced p99. Marking incident resolved for now.

oncall-bot: incident 2025-04-12-01 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

Anna (SRE): thanks everyone. Sam, keep me posted if customer sees any regressions. We'll follow up with postmortem and preventative controls. :thumbsup:
